hero.title: Toll Brothers Digital Studio
hero.subtitle: Showcase of four home customization tools for the Toll Brothers Studio app.

sections.intro: Toll Brothers traditionally relied on outdated digital modules and PDFs to deliver home customization options. The new **Digital Studio** app is a comprehensive digital home customization platform. I led end-to-end design on four major modules: **Floor Plan Configurator**, the **Furniture Planner**, and **Digital Catalog**, and the internal-facing **Collection Builder** to curate sets for the Digital Catalog.

frames.intro: The digital Floor Plan Configurator helps homebuyers understand and pre-select architectural customization options. Research reported that homebuyers found the old module difficult to use and needed in-person guidance to understand options.
frames.text:
1. Failed to communicate complex option dependencies.
2. Relied on trial-and-error with dense tooltips.
3. Built on desktop-first principles with limited mobile support.

To understand the full scope of option relationships, I researched 80 floor plans with the most complicated setups.

frames.header: New Floor Plan Option Visualization System
frames.text: I designed a modular component system that grouped and visualized dependencies and constraints. Based on the floor plan research, I adapted the design to accomodate for complex edge-cases such as combination and assymetric constraint groups. Stakeholders approved the framework after I demonstrated. Then, I redesigned the module on mobile-first principles.

sections.intro: On the internal product side, the product team would curate features for designer-appointed collections using PDFs. As the company pivoted to more pre-selected builds and quick move-in homes, the product team needed an internal tool to construct collections of products at scale. I partnered with a senior developer and designed the MVP wireframes from scratch. For a desktop-only tool, these were the basic requirements:

items: Upload new features to the system.

figures.caption: Collection Builder main page showing collection cards with mosaic feature thumbnails. Cards are categorized by publish states.

A single collection showing added features categorized by location. A general Select Features button is in the top-right corner, and each location has a smaller location-specific Select Features button.
Select Features shows selected and recommended features. The gray indicator in the top-right corner communicates selection state and enables location changes.
The Upload Feature appears as a tab in Select Features. Product teams can upload spreadsheets of features. There are duplication guardrails.

blocks.text: During the build process, my developer partner and I fleshed out additional management-focused requirements, such as multi-upload, duplicate prevention, and publish states. The demo for this project received internal approval and was added to the backlog.

sections.intro: I revisited the Design Your Own Home module to add a mobile-optimized furniture planner function. The old design includes a furniture planner available only on desktop. To elegantly add a furniture planner to mobile, I reduced its prominence, added a variant-selection state, and removed resizing features that do not apply to furniture with preset sizes.

figures.caption: The furniture planner button is placed in the bottom-right corner.
Users can select from a horizontal carousel of furniture categories.
Users can place a default piece and then move, rotate, delete, or change variants.
Users can swap furniture variants in a dedicated variant-swap state.

sections.intro: The digital catalog is an ongoing team effort to replace PDF catalogs with a digital app experience. Users take a style survey, receive a recommended curated set of finishes, and adjust the selection. I designed several key screens with feature scalability in mind, creating a reusable selection pattern for cabinets that can be repurposed for other features like flooring.

figures.caption: Style Survey prefills the majority of hardware and finishes. The flow is optimized for refinement over selection.
The Cabinet tab in the Kitchen selection flow balances several required elements: navigation, visualizer, stacked cabinet toggle, zoning, filters, selection, return option, and confirmation bar.
Flooring exists as its own section, allowing users to compare kitchen and bath flooring, and accommodating grout selection.
Grout selection expands the bottom confirmation bar into a full bottom sheet.
